children: , the biotechnology company, said its experimental Sjogren's disease drug dazodalibep met the main goal of a Phase 3 trial. Shares rose about 0.2% to $406.85 at 11.14am ET time on Thursday. The trial news is promising, but the stock's modest move suggests investors want the full data before assigning the drug much more value.

The roughly 621-patient OASIZ 301 study found an improvement in systemic disease activity at week 48, with benefits appearing as early as week four, according to Amgen's results. The company said the most common adverse events were generally mild or moderate and that few patients stopped treatment because of them. Amgen has released only top-line findings so far; the detailed results will matter.

There is a real opening here: Sjogren's disease has no FDA-approved treatment. But Reuters reported that analysts still need the full trial data, while Amgen's separate OASIZ 303 study is expected to finish in the fourth quarter. At $406.85, the shares stand 10.72% above the $367.47 GF Value estimate. That premium leaves room for a successful drugbut raises the stakes for the next readout.

title: Amgen Gains as Sjogren's Drug Clears Phase 3
